sections.h2: Where to take property tax questions
sections.html:
Owners deal with two Newnan offices. For bills and payments, call the Tax Commissioner (87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100) at 770-254-2670. For values and homestead claims, call the Assessor's Office (37 Perry Street) at 770-254-2680.

Weekday counter hours at the commissioner's are 8am to 4:30pm. Two elected bodies, the county commissioners and the school board, choose separate millage rates, while value disputes go to a board the grand jury names. Deed copies come from the Clerk of Superior Court in the Coweta County Justice Center at 72 Greenville Street, 770-254-2690.

  • Value or exemption question: Assessor's Office.
  • Bill, payoff or lien question: Tax Commissioner.
  • Deed copy: Clerk of Superior Court.

Southwest of Atlanta in the Georgia Piedmont, Coweta counts as Metro Atlanta. Newnan serves as seat and largest city. The five cities are Newnan, Senoia, Grantville, Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills, the last two reaching into Fulton County.

The county grew from 127,317 people in 2010 to 146,158 in 2020, with 160,240 estimated for July 2025. Owners make up 78.4% of households. A typical owned home is valued at $357,500, and rent averages $1,488 a month. In a market this owner-heavy, a tax line is routine on closing statements.

Bills go out October 1 and are due December 1, so you get at least 60 days. Should your printed bill show a different date, follow the printed one.

Pay in the drive-through drop box, by card online (the card company charges a fee), or by mail with a postmark no later than the due date. If the office is shut on the due date, you have until the next business day.

Broader Georgia property tax questions can go to the state Department of Revenue, local government services division, at dor.georgia.gov.

  • January 1: ownership and use on this date fix the year's tax.
  • Through April 1: returns, first-year homestead filings and special program applications.
  • April 1: mobile and manufactured home tax, with a location decal issued after payment.
  • October 1: bills go in the mail.
  • December 1: due date for land, buildings and personal property.

Interest runs monthly at prime plus three percentage points. A 5% penalty hits at day 120, then again every 120 days, ending at 20%. No penalty applies to homesteaded bills under $500.

About a month after nonpayment the commissioner can file a FiFa lien on the General Execution Docket at the superior court clerk's office. That lien can follow your credit for seven years or longer. Delinquent notices only go out occasionally, so phone for today's balance before mailing a check.

Mobile and manufactured homes face a sharper risk. Miss the April 1 payment and permit, and the result can be a 10% penalty, a citation to Coweta County State Court, or a sale of the home.

sections.h2: Who pays when a house changes hands
sections.html:
A lien is recorded against whoever owned the property on January 1. When a bill arrives after you sold, give it to the buyer. The lien shifts only if the commissioner is shown a contract or closing statement within 90 days after the due date.

When your closing prorated the tax, deliver the settlement statement to the Newnan Station Drive office. With it on file, an unpaid bill produces a lien against the new owner.

Timing matters. October is when bills are mailed, so a spring or summer closing normally comes before that year's bill exists, and the title company has to estimate. Use last year's total from the commissioner as a benchmark and ask the closer how the estimate was built.

A bill covers the whole tax year, not just the months after the sale, so write the tax split into the contract in plain words. That way both sides and the closer work from the same page. At the closing table, expect to hand over your latest bill and any assessment notice, and your payoff from the commissioner should be on the settlement statement. A cash buyer will still follow the same split, but closes without waiting on a lender's appraisal, so the tax estimate is often settled sooner.

sections.h2: Before you sign a listing agreement
sections.html: Phone the Tax Commissioner at 770-254-2670 to learn what is owed on the parcel, FiFa included. If you hold a homestead exemption, plan to tell the Assessor's Office once the sale closes, because the exemption belongs to the occupant and the buyer files a new claim. Look at your assessment notice too. With 45 days to appeal, a notice received in the weeks before listing is worth acting on promptly.

The deadline is 45 days after the assessment notice. Begin with a written appeal on the state's uniform form, filed with the Board of Assessors and naming the route you choose. Valid grounds include taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

Coweta County appeal routes
RouteBest suited toWhat follows
Equalization boardMost homeownersHearing, then Superior Court if needed
Hearing officerNon-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or moreDecision, then Superior Court if needed
ArbitrationOwners holding a current certified appraisalHearing within 30 days; the ruling is final

On the equalization route, the assessors may revise the value and mail a new notice, and you then have 30 days to appeal that. If they leave the value alone, the appeal advances to a hearing automatically. With arbitration, the assessors have 45 days to acknowledge the appeal, and if they turn down your appraisal they must certify the case to the Clerk of Superior Court.

To claim homestead, you must have owned the house and lived there on January 1 and get the application in by April 1 of the first year. Later filings take effect the next year. The assessors decide each claim and you can appeal a denial, but homestead cannot be claimed on a second property.

Local exemptions in Coweta replace the state amount whenever they are larger. Ask the assessors what proof they need for age, income or military service. After approval it renews on its own until you move or ownership changes.

  • Deferral: owners 62 and over with gross household income of $15,000 or less can put tax off until ownership changes or the balance plus interest hits 85% of fair market value.
  • Agricultural use: qualifying farmland is assessed at 30% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection: 10-year or 15-year covenants.
  • Historic property and Hazardous Site Reuse: preferential assessment, applied for during the first four months of the year it begins.

Anyone buying an enrolled tract should check with the assessors on whether the covenant carries over.

faqs.q: Who sends my Coweta County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner, 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan. Mailing is October 1, and the office phone is 770-254-2670.

faqs.q: Is December 1 the due date for every Coweta County bill?
faqs.a: It applies to land, buildings and personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1. Your printed bill shows which date is yours.

faqs.q: Can a hearing officer decide a Coweta County homestead appeal?
faqs.a: No. That route is reserved for the value of non-homestead real property at $1,000,000 or more.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my deed in Coweta County?
faqs.a: Ask the Clerk of Superior Court at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, GA 30263, or call 770-254-2690.

faqs.q: Does every unpaid Coweta County bill draw a penalty?
faqs.a: Not a homesteaded bill under $500. Others pick up a 5% penalty at 120 days, again every 120 days, capped at 20%.
